memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Adah gave birth to Jabal; he was the father of those who live in tents and raise livestock. His brother's name was Jubal; he was the father of all who play stringed instruments and pipes. - Gen 4:20-21 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Something surprising happens in Cain's line. Out of this family, so far from God, come the pioneers of herding, of tent-dwelling, of music with strings and pipes. Culture, industry and art are born here. It is a reminder that human creativity and skill are real gifts - even among people who are not walking with God.

This is what theologians call common grace. God generously gives talent, beauty and ability to all people, believers and unbelievers alike, because "every good and perfect gift is from above" (Jas 1:17). The music that stirs your soul, the crafts that fill the world with beauty, the skills that build civilisation - all of it ultimately traces back to a generous Creator, even when the maker does not acknowledge Him.

For us, this brings both gratitude and challenge. We can enjoy and celebrate the good gifts of human culture, seeing God's fingerprints even in unexpected places. And we can offer our own talents back to the One who gave them.

The real question is not whether we are gifted, but whom we serve with our gifts. Jabal's family made music without God; how much more should we, who know Him, use every talent to His glory (Col 3:23)?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What gifts and skills has God given you?
- Are you using your talents for God's glory or only your own?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, every good gift comes from You. Thank You for the talents You have placed in this world, and help me use mine to honour You.
